title: Mexico’s Federal Judiciary Reports 88% of Cases Resolved in One Year
author: El Chamuco Editorial Staff
content:
_This article originally appeared in the[September 8, 2026 edition of El
Chamuco](https://elchamuco.com.mx/2026/09/08/poder-judicial-88-por-ciento-
expedientes-resueltos/), an independent Mexican political magazine._

The Federal Judiciary resolved **13,231 of the 15,051 case files** received or
inherited during the first 12 months of its new era, reported the president of
the Supreme Court of Justice of the Nation, Hugo Aguilar Ortiz.

The figure represents **88 percent** of the total number of matters.

Aguilar presented the assessment during the ceremony “A Year of Real and True
Justice: A New Way of Understanding and Delivering Justice.”

## The Court Modernizes Its Processes

Among the actions undertaken by the Supreme Court are new case-management
systems, the expansion of the electronic case file, and rules for drafting
final rulings and votes.

Mechanisms for the random assignment of cases were also introduced to improve
the efficiency, transparency, and traceability of proceedings.

The Supreme Court received 10,000 requests for assistance during its first
year.

The Federal Judiciary also opened new intercultural legal-aid offices and
launched itinerant programs and regional oversight offices.

## Savings of 4.7 Billion Pesos Reported

Aguilar Ortiz reported that spending-rationalization policies made it possible
to achieve savings of **more than 4.7 billion pesos**.

He also highlighted the expansion of the Public Defender’s Office, the use of
digital signatures, and specialized training.

“Those who elected us have the right to oversee us every day, because
resources must be objectively rationalized in order to deliver quality
justice,” he said.

> “Those who elected us have the right to oversee us every day, because
> resources must be objectively rationalized in order to deliver quality
> justice.”
>
> Hugo Aguilar Ortiz, President of the Supreme Court

## Judicial Discipline and Political Violence

The Judicial Disciplinary Tribunal opened six regional oversight offices and
adopted a qualitative model to evaluate the performance of judges.

The Electoral Tribunal (TEPJF) also strengthened its Public Defender’s Office
and specialized services to handle cases of gender-based political violence
against women.
